_about: Approved by Nav on 2026-11-20 (E0, prompts 43–44). Mars's 30 fun facts for the Destination file card and /destinations/mars, one a day. Every fact was checked on 2026-11-20 against the NASA page in 'source'; 'quote' is the supporting text from that page. None repeats a milestone fact (content/milestones.json). This file is the template for the other destinations: same fields, 30 facts, a source and quote for each.

facts.fact: A day on Mars is called a sol, short for solar day.
facts.quote: Martian days are called sols — short for "solar day."

facts.fact: Mars spins once every 24.6 hours, about 40 minutes longer than a day on Earth.
facts.quote: it completes one rotation every 24.6 hours, which is very similar to one day on Earth (23.9 hours).

facts.fact: A year on Mars lasts 687 Earth days.
facts.quote: A year on Mars lasts 669.6 sols, which is the same as 687 Earth days.

facts.fact: Mars is about half the size of Earth, with a radius of 3,390 km.
facts.quote: With a radius of 2,106 miles (3,390 kilometers), Mars is about half the size of Earth.

facts.fact: Mars is small, but its surface has nearly the same area as all of Earth's dry land.
facts.quote: its surface has nearly the same area as Earth's dry land.

facts.fact: Sunlight takes about 13 minutes to reach Mars.
facts.quote: it takes sunlight 13 minutes to travel from the Sun to Mars.

facts.fact: Mars is on average 228 million km from the Sun, 1.5 times as far as Earth.
facts.quote: From an average distance of 142 million miles (228 million kilometers), Mars is 1.5 astronomical units away from the Sun.

facts.fact: Mars is tilted 25 degrees, close to Earth's 23.4, so it has seasons too.
facts.quote: Mars' axis of rotation is tilted 25 degrees … Earth, which has an axial tilt of 23.4 degrees.

facts.fact: Seasons on Mars last longer than ours, because a Martian year is longer.
facts.quote: Mars has distinct seasons, but they last longer than seasons here on Earth

facts.fact: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, that may be captured asteroids.
facts.quote: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, that may be captured asteroids.

facts.fact: Phobos and Deimos are potato-shaped: too small for gravity to pull them round.
facts.quote: They're potato-shaped because they have too little mass for gravity to make them spherical.

facts.fact: The moons are named after the horses that pulled the chariot of Ares, the Greek god of war.
facts.quote: The moons get their names from the horses that pulled the chariot of the Greek god of war, Ares

facts.fact: Asaph Hall discovered both of Mars' moons in 1877.
facts.quote: Asaph Hall discovered both the Red Planet's moons in 1877.

facts.fact: Phobos is creeping closer to Mars, by about 1.8 metres every hundred years.
facts.quote: It's nearing Mars at a rate of six feet (1.8 meters) every hundred years.

facts.fact: In about 50 million years Phobos will crash into Mars or break up into a ring.
facts.quote: the moon will either crash into Mars in 50 million years or break up into a ring.

facts.fact: Stickney, the biggest crater on Phobos, takes up about half of the moon's surface.
facts.quote: Stickney crater is about 6-miles (9.7 kilometers) wide, and takes up about half the moon's surface.

facts.fact: Deimos goes round Mars once every 30 hours.
facts.quote: Deimos orbits Mars every 30 hours.

facts.fact: Deimos looks smoother than Phobos because loose dirt fills many of its craters.
facts.quote: covered in loose dirt that often fills the craters on its surface, making it appear smoother than pockmarked Phobos.

facts.fact: Olympus Mons is the biggest volcano in the Solar System, more than 40 km tall from base to summit.
facts.quote: Olympus Mons stands more than 25 miles (that's more than 132,000 feet, or 40 kilometers) tall from base to summit

facts.fact: The base of Olympus Mons covers an area as big as the US state of Arizona.
facts.quote: with the base covering an area as large as the state of Arizona.

facts.fact: Valles Marineris, the Solar System's biggest canyon, is about 3,870 km long: long enough to stretch from California to New York.
facts.quote: extends about 2,400 miles (3,870 kilometers) in length … long enough to stretch from California to New York

facts.fact: At its deepest, Valles Marineris drops about 9.3 km from rim to floor.
facts.quote: descends about 5.8 miles (9.3 kilometers) at its deepest, from the rim to the canyon floor.

facts.fact: Sunsets on Mars look blue: fine dust lets blue light through near the Sun.

source.label: NASA: Sunset in Mars' Gale Crater

facts.quote: Dust in the Martian atmosphere has fine particles that permit blue light to penetrate the atmosphere more efficiently

facts.fact: Mars looks red because iron in its rocks and dust has rusted.
facts.quote: The reason Mars looks reddish is due to oxidization — or rusting — of iron in the rocks

facts.fact: The ancient Romans named Mars after their god of war, because its red colour looked like blood.
facts.quote: Mars was named by the ancient Romans for their god of war because its reddish color was reminiscent of blood.

facts.fact: The ancient Egyptians called Mars "Her Desher", which means "the red one".
facts.quote: the Egyptians called it "Her Desher," meaning "the red one."

facts.fact: Mars can be as warm as 20 °C or as cold as about -153 °C.
facts.quote: The temperature on Mars can be as high as 70 degrees Fahrenheit (20 degrees Celsius) or as low as about -225 degrees Fahrenheit (-153 degrees Celsius).

facts.fact: Martian dust storms can cover much of the planet, and the dust can take months to settle.
facts.quote: winds on Mars are strong enough to create dust storms that cover much of the planet … it can be months before all of the dust settles.

facts.fact: Viking 1 sent the first pictures from the surface of Mars after landing on 20 July 1976.
facts.quote: until July 20, 1976, when NASA's Viking 1 lander touched down safely and began transmitting the first images from the surface

facts.fact: On 19 April 2021 the Ingenuity helicopter made the first powered flight on another planet.
facts.quote: took to the Martian air for its initial flight on April 19, 2021— the first powered flight on another planet.
